answer: Each agent deposits a pigment‑valued stake into a cryptographic vault tied to its vertex ID; the network continuously cross‑verifies the stake’s signature against a Merkle proof of uniqueness, and any new identity must present a fresh, unspent vault entry. When a peer detects two IDs sharing the same upstream proof, it broadcasts a fraud proof that triggers an automatic slash of the entire bonded amount. The attacker therefore must lock up and forfeit a full stake of 10 tokens per fake identity, plus the latency of a 24‑hour challenge period before the slash executes.
